skills.name: audit-refactor-project
skills.description: Whole-repository audit and refactor for simplicity and performance: finds duplicated ownership across features, repairs root causes upstream, removes speculative validation, fallbacks and error suppression, simplifies over-engineered APIs and module boundaries, finds evidence-backed performance problems (redundant work, N+1 and I/O in loops, needless copies, hot-path waste), and verifies with the full format/lint/type/test/build chain and before/after measurement. Reports user-visible feature removals as candidates without implementing them. Use whenever the user asks to audit, review, simplify, de-duplicate, optimize, speed up or clean up an entire project or several modules, even without the word "refactor" (e.g. "audit this repo", "simplify the architecture", "find duplicated logic across features", "why is this system slow", "remove dead code and over-defensive checks", "audit/refactor/optimize repo"). Not for single-bug fixes, new features, single-file cleanup or small local refactors (use tidy-code).

skills.name: code-analysis
skills.description: Read-only, evidence-bounded analysis of a specific function, flow or module along one named dimension: performance (where time, memory or I/O goes for a stated scenario and scale) or reentrancy/concurrency (whether an interleaving can actually produce a wrong state). Confirms or refutes a suspicion and reports only findings backed by a cost calculation, a concrete execution sequence or a measurement; "no significant problem found" is a valid result. Use when the user asks "why is this so slow", "analyze performance", "is this a performance issue", "is there a reentrancy, concurrency, or race issue", "where is the time going", "can this re-enter". Does not edit code, hunt bugs or give generic advice. Not for implementing fixes (use tidy-code) or whole-repository audits (use audit-refactor-project).

skills.name: concise-plan-docs
skills.description: Write, revise and maintain implementation plans and related project documents as a non-redundant system where every rule has one authoritative owner: normative contract (specs, numbered decisions), action plan, analysis, and execution record. Use whenever the user asks to create or change a plan, spec, contract, numbered decision (e.g. "D12"), acceptance gate, task board or progress record, or to deduplicate or reorganize such documents, e.g. "update the plan document", "revise this decision", "adjust the plan to the new decision", "organize the planning documents", "write up the implementation plan", "record what we did". Bounded edits stay bounded: change the authority and only the active text that would implement the old rule. Not for README/API reference, code comments, or general prose editing.

skills.name: decision-lock
skills.description: Protect user-approved architectural direction while actively auditing and improving plans, documents and implementation details inside that boundary. Use when the user wants flaws, omissions, contradictions, sequencing problems or overdesign found and fixed without reopening settled decisions; when decisions or phase boundaries are frozen, agreed, authoritative or already decided; when the user says follow the agreed plan, preserve the overall direction, maintain consistency, do not redesign, optimize within the agreed direction, "don't redesign"; or when audit/refactor skills must stay subordinate to prior decisions. Not for greenfield design where nothing is decided yet.

skills.name: tidy-code
skills.description: Write, change or review code in a bounded area with the least final machinery and no wasted work: fix problems at the source, trust established internal invariants, reuse the project's canonical utilities/dependencies, delete forwarding wrappers and speculative guards/fallbacks, remove redundant computation and I/O, and keep caller-facing APIs to one direct call per intent. Use for local refactoring, simplification, optimization or a final readability pass on a module, file or feature, and whenever the user says "clean up", "simplify", "tidy", "optimize", "too slow", "too defensive", "too many layers", "simplify/tidy/optimize/remove redundant guards". Not for repository-wide audits or architecture decisions (use audit-refactor-project) or for plain bug fixes.
